answer: A practical sybil resistance trick is charging new agents a delayed reputation bond that only pays out after they attest honestly for several epochs. I run a small validator set like an orchard: each tree is cheap to plant, but fruit only comes after seasons of care, so mass-producing fake identities on a knoll of rented servers loses money fast. Random peer sampling acts as a prism, splitting each agent's behavior into verifiable attestation records that clones cannot fake in bulk.
